questions.question:
D1 — Add gstack skill routing rules to CLAUDE.md?
Project/branch/task: main branch, plan-design-review of PLAN.md (Settings Page UI redesign).
ELI10: gstack works best when your project's CLAUDE.md includes skill routing rules, so that when you say "review this design" or "ship it" the right skill fires without you naming it. This is a one-time onboarding prompt for this project. Since we're in plan mode, if you pick A I'll append the section and commit only after the review finishes and plan mode exits.
Stakes if we pick wrong: pick B and you invoke skills by hand forever (re-enable is one config command); pick A and CLAUDE.md gains ~15 lines.
Recommendation: A because routing rules make the skill set discoverable at no runtime cost.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Net: convenience of auto-routing vs. a small addition to a checked-in file.

options.label: Add routing rules to CLAUDE.md (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Requests like "review this plan" auto-route to the matching skill. ✅ One-time setup, applies to every future session in this repo. ❌ Adds a ~15-line section to CLAUDE.md and a commit (deferred until plan mode exits).

options.label: No thanks, I'll invoke skills manually
options.description: ✅ CLAUDE.md stays exactly as it is, nothing committed. ✅ Re-enable any time with one gstack-config command. ❌ You have to name skills explicitly every time.

questions.question:
D2 — Review all 7 design dimensions, or focus on specific areas?
Project/branch/task: main branch, plan-design-review of PLAN.md (Settings Page UI redesign).
ELI10: I've rated this plan 6/10 on design completeness. The behavior spec is excellent; the five listed visual gaps (Save hierarchy, spacing rhythm, error contrast, label sizes, Save pending state) have no committed values yet, even though DESIGN.md already defines every one of them. You asked for all seven dimensions and text-only; this confirms that scope before I start the passes, each of which will surface findings for your individual approval.
Stakes if we pick wrong: a narrower focus is faster but leaves untouched dimensions (e.g. AI-slop risk, journey) at whatever score they land.
Recommendation: A because you asked for all seven and the plan is small enough that a full pass is cheap.
Completeness: A=10/10, B=6/10
Net: full coverage vs. speed on a plan small enough that speed barely matters.

options.label: All 7 dimensions (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Every dimension gets rated and every gap gets its own decision, matching your request. ✅ Catches the states the plan text still leaves implicit, not just the five it already lists. ❌ More approval questions (roughly one per finding, expect 8-12).

options.label: Only the 5 listed gaps
options.description: ✅ Fastest path: resolve Visual Hierarchy, Spacing, Color, Typography, Motion against DESIGN.md tokens. ✅ Fewer questions to answer. ❌ Skips Information Architecture, Journey, AI-slop, Interaction-state coverage beyond what's listed.

questions.question:
D3 — Enable cross-project learnings search?
Project/branch/task: main branch, plan-design-review of PLAN.md (Settings Page UI redesign).
ELI10: gstack can search learnings saved from your other projects on this machine to find patterns that might apply here (e.g. a form-state pitfall found in another repo). Everything stays local; no data leaves your machine. One-time setting.
Stakes if we pick wrong: enable it on a machine with multiple client codebases and one client's notes could surface while working on another; keep it scoped and you lose reuse across your own projects.
Recommendation: A because for a solo developer the reuse is free and local.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Net: cross-repo pattern reuse vs. strict per-project isolation.

options.label: Enable cross-project learnings (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Pitfalls and patterns from your other repos surface in this review automatically. ✅ Fully local; one config flag, reversible any time. ❌ Not ideal if you work across multiple client codebases where cross-contamination matters.

options.label: Keep learnings project-scoped only
options.description: ✅ Strict isolation: only this project's learnings are ever searched. ✅ Safe default for consultants juggling client repos. ❌ You lose reuse of lessons learned elsewhere on this machine.

questions.question:
Issue 1 (Pass 1, Info Arch) — Make Save the visible primary action?
Project/branch/task: main branch, plan-design-review of PLAN.md (Settings Page UI redesign).
ELI10: The header has four buttons that all look the same. A user scanning the page can't tell which one commits their work and which one throws it away. DESIGN.md already decides this: Save is the only filled primary (#1d4ed8, white text); Reset, Cancel and Export are neutral ghost buttons. The plan lists this gap but never commits to the token.
Stakes if we pick wrong: users mis-tap Reset or Cancel beside Save on a 320px row and hit a discard dialog they didn't want; primary action recognition is the 3-second scan test.
Principle: Hierarchy as service — what should the user see first? The one button that stores their work.
Recommendation: 1A because DESIGN.md already specifies the exact treatment and the Button component already has the role.
Completeness: 1A=10/10, 1B=7/10, 1C=2/10
Effort 1A: (human: ~1h / CC: ~5min).
Net: one token swap on one button vs. leaving the header ambiguous.

options.label: 1A Save filled primary, others ghost (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Save uses the existing filled primary role (#1d4ed8 bg, white text); Reset/Cancel/Export use the existing neutral ghost role. ✅ Matches DESIGN.md exactly; no new styles, existing Button component. ❌ None beyond doing the work; disabled/pending appearance of the filled button must still read as inactive (already the existing disabled style).

options.label: 1B Save primary, Export also emphasized
options.description: ✅ Signals Export as a safe, non-destructive action distinct from Reset/Cancel. ❌ Violates DESIGN.md (Save is the only filled primary) and re-splits attention across two emphasized buttons.

options.label: 1C Keep all four uniform (decline)
options.description: ✅ Zero work now. ❌ Leaves the documented gap open, fails the 3-second scan test, and contradicts DESIGN.md; Pass 1 stays at 7/10.

questions.question:
Issue 2 (Pass 2, States) — Save pending feedback: which pattern?
Project/branch/task: main branch, plan-design-review of PLAN.md (Settings Page UI redesign).
ELI10: Save takes 2-5 seconds and the page shows nothing. Users either click again (already blocked, so it feels broken) or assume it failed. DESIGN.md's established pending pattern is an inline spinner beside “Saving…” inside the disabled Save button with aria-busy=true and reduced-motion support; it's the same pattern the plan already accepts for Export (“Exporting…”). The plan's own text “do not repeat Saving… in the status live region” assumes this label exists.
Stakes if we pick wrong: a skeleton would hide the fields the user just edited (and the plan says preserve unsaved values and don't move focus), so it fights the accepted contract.
Principle: Trust is earned at the pixel level — the 2-5s wait is the moment the user decides whether their preferences were stored.
Recommendation: 2A because it is the existing pattern, matches Export exactly, and keeps focus and field values in place.
Completeness: 2A=10/10, 2B=4/10, 2C=1/10
Effort 2A: (human: ~2h / CC: ~10min).
Net: reuse the exact Export pattern on Save vs. inventing a second pending idiom.

options.label: 2A Inline spinner + “Saving…” in Save button (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Existing spinner beside “Saving…” inside Save, aria-busy=true, aria-disabled + activation guard, focus stays put; reduced motion swaps spinner animation for a static indicator. ✅ Identical to the accepted Export pattern, so users learn it once. ❌ Label change widens the button above 640px unless width is reserved (surfaced as its own issue in Pass 6).

options.label: 2B Skeleton over the form while saving
options.description: ✅ Very visible “something is happening” signal. ❌ Hides the user's edits, conflicts with “preserve unsaved values” and “do not move focus”, and contradicts DESIGN.md's established pending pattern.

options.label: 2C Leave as is (decline)
options.description: ✅ No work. ❌ 2-5s frozen page remains; Pass 2 stays at 7/10 and Pass 3 (journey) keeps its trust break.

questions.question:
Issue 3 (Pass 5, Design System) — Error message colors: adopt DESIGN.md error tokens?
Project/branch/task: main branch, plan-design-review of PLAN.md (Settings Page UI redesign).
ELI10: Error text is currently red on light pink at roughly 3:1 contrast. WCAG AA needs 4.5:1 for body-size text, so low-vision users and anyone on a dim phone screen struggle to read the one message telling them why their save failed. DESIGN.md specifies error.text #991b1b on error.surface #fef2f2 (about 7.5:1) with an icon and explicit text, so status never rides on color alone.
Stakes if we pick wrong: the recovery moment in the journey (step 4/6b) stays the least legible thing on the page; it's also a straightforward AA failure.
Principle: Accessibility is not optional; specify contrast in the plan or it won't exist.
Recommendation: 3A because the tokens exist, exceed AA, and apply to field errors, ErrorSummary and the network/export error row with one change.
Completeness: 3A=10/10, 3B=6/10, 3C=0/10
Effort 3A: (human: ~1h / CC: ~5min).
Net: one token pair across every error surface vs. an AA failure at the recovery moment.

options.label: 3A #991b1b on #fef2f2 + icon + text (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Applies DESIGN.md error.text/error.surface to field errors, ErrorSummary and the network/export error row; contrast ~7.5:1, well past AA. ✅ Icon plus explicit text means the state never depends on color. ❌ Must be verified on every error surface including the 320px wrapped Retry row (add to verification).

options.label: 3B Darken text only, keep current surface
options.description: ✅ Smaller visual change from today's look. ❌ Invents a token not in DESIGN.md; still needs a measured contrast check and leaves ErrorSummary/field errors possibly inconsistent.

options.label: 3C Leave as is (decline)
options.description: ✅ No work. ❌ Ships a WCAG AA failure on the page's most important recovery message; Pass 5 and Pass 6 stay below 8.

questions.question:
Issue 4 (Pass 5, Design System) — Label type sizes: adopt DESIGN.md's two roles?
Project/branch/task: main branch, plan-design-review of PLAN.md (Settings Page UI redesign).
ELI10: Form labels currently render at 14px, 16px and 18px with no rule for which is which. Three sizes on four fields reads as noise, and the 14px ones fall under the 16px floor for body text. DESIGN.md defines exactly two roles: 16px for body, form labels and helper text; 20px for the Profile/Notifications h2 headings. The plan says “two sizes would suffice” but never names them.
Stakes if we pick wrong: an implementer picks sizes ad hoc; 14px labels stay hard to read on phones and the hierarchy between heading and label stays muddy.
Principle: Specificity over vibes; name the scale or it won't exist.
Recommendation: 4A because DESIGN.md already commits to these two roles and the font family is unchanged.
Completeness: 4A=10/10, 4B=5/10, 4C=0/10
Effort 4A: (human: ~1h / CC: ~5min).
Net: two named sizes vs. three unnamed ones.

options.label: 4A 16px labels/body/helper, 20px h2 (recommended)
options.description: ✅ All labels, helper text, status text, error text and inputs at 16px; Profile and Notifications h2 at 20px; h1 keeps its existing page-title size. ✅ Removes the sub-16px labels and gives one clear step between heading and field. ❌ Any existing 18px label loses its emphasis; if one was intentional it needs a reason (none is recorded).

options.label: 4B Keep 16/18px, drop only 14px
options.description: ✅ Fixes the under-16px readability problem with the smallest change. ❌ Leaves a third size DESIGN.md doesn't define and keeps the label-vs-heading hierarchy unclear.

options.label: 4C Leave as is (decline)
options.description: ✅ No work. ❌ Three sizes, 14px body text below the floor; Pass 4 and Pass 5 stay below 10.

questions.question:
Issue 5 (Pass 5, Design System) — Vertical rhythm: adopt DESIGN.md's 8px scale?
Project/branch/task: main branch, plan-design-review of PLAN.md (Settings Page UI redesign).
ELI10: Gaps between parts of the form are 16px in one place, 24px in another, 32px in a third, with no rule. The eye reads inconsistent gaps as separate groups, so Profile and Notifications don't feel like siblings and fields don't clearly belong to their heading. DESIGN.md sets an 8px base: 32px between sections, 24px between field groups, 8px from label to input. The plan names the gap but not the values.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Gestalt proximity breaks; the implementer eyeballs spacing and the form keeps looking assembled rather than designed.
Principle: Visual hierarchy is everything: related things visually grouped, nested things visually contained.
Recommendation: 5A because the scale is already written down and maps directly onto the existing section/field structure.
Completeness: 5A=10/10, 5B=6/10, 5C=0/10
Effort 5A: (human: ~1h / CC: ~5min).
Net: three named values on an 8px grid vs. three arbitrary ones.

options.label: 5A 32px sections / 24px field groups / 8px label-to-input (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Header → status slot → Profile → Notifications separated by 32px; fields within a fieldset by 24px; label to its input by 8px; error/Retry row gap stays 8px. ✅ Every value is a multiple of 8, so the page reads as one rhythm at 320px and at 640px. ❌ The 8px error-row gap and the 640px reflow gaps need to be checked against the same scale in verification.

options.label: 5B Normalize to a single 24px gap everywhere
options.description: ✅ One number, trivially consistent. ❌ Flattens the section-vs-field distinction DESIGN.md wants (sections should read as bigger breaks than fields) and diverges from the written scale.

options.label: 5C Leave as is (decline)
options.description: ✅ No work. ❌ Rhythm stays 16/24/32 at random; Pass 5 stays below 8.

questions.question:
Issue 6 (Pass 6, Responsive) — Save button width during “Saving…” above 640px?
Project/branch/task: main branch, plan-design-review of PLAN.md (Settings Page UI redesign).
ELI10: Above 640px the four header buttons share one row. When Save's label changes to a spinner plus “Saving…”, the button gets wider and shoves Reset, Cancel and Export to the right, then they jump back when the request settles. Neither the plan nor DESIGN.md says whether Save reserves that width. At 640px and below Save is full-width, so nothing moves there.
Stakes if we pick wrong: a 2-5 second layout jump right under the pointer, on every save, and a pointer parked over Export can land on nothing; “would I notice?” says yes.
Principle: Invisible is perfect: the highest compliment is not noticing the design.
Recommendation: 6A because a reserved min-width is a one-line CSS rule that keeps the row still and needs no new pattern.
Completeness: 6A=10/10, 6B=8/10, 6C=3/10
Effort 6A: (human: ~30min / CC: ~2min).
Net: reserve a few extra pixels permanently vs. a visible jump on every save.

options.label: 6A Reserve min-width for the pending label (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Save's min-width above 640px equals its rendered width with spinner + “Saving…”, so Reset/Cancel/Export never move during a request. ✅ Still fits the 640px form width; below 640px Save is already full-width. ❌ Idle Save is a few pixels wider than its text needs, and the width must be re-measured if the label copy changes.

options.label: 6B Show spinner only, keep “Save” label
options.description: ✅ Minimal width change; the row barely moves. ❌ Diverges from DESIGN.md's “Saving…” pattern and from Export's “Exporting…”, and under reduced motion a static spinner alone is a weak signal.

options.label: 6C Accept the layout shift
options.description: ✅ No extra rule to maintain. ❌ Buttons jump on every save for 2-5s and snap back; feels unpolished and can move a target from under the pointer.

answers.Issue 6 (Pass 6, Responsive) \u2014 Save: 6A Reserve min-width for the pending label (recommended)
